Infectious mononucleosis is a systemic manifestation of EBV, but the patient has CNS involvement, making EBV Meningoencephalitis (R1) a more specific and comprehensive diagnosis.
Meningoencephalitis is a general term for inflammation of the brain and meninges. R1 (EBV Meningoencephalitis) is more specific as it identifies the causative agent.
Cerebral vasculitis is a distinct pathological process, potentially a complication, but not the primary diagnosis of infection.
Viral meningitis is a less specific diagnosis than EBV Meningoencephalitis (R1), as the causative agent (EBV) and brain involvement are identified in R1.
EBV Encephalitis is a component of EBV Meningoencephalitis (R1), which also includes meningeal involvement.
This candidate represents the most specific and comprehensive diagnosis given the evidence of both meningeal and brain inflammation caused by EBV.
